_comment: Feedback shown in the mock test after a question is answered: 'right' when the answer is correct, 'wrong' when it is wrong or skipped. Keys are question ids from docs/data/questions.json; 'question' is only a reminder of which question it is. Options are shuffled in the test, so refer to answers by content, never by letter.

e6548e18f3.question: An e-commerce company wants to group customers based on purchasing behavior without predef...
e6548e18f3.right: No predefined labels means unsupervised learning, and clustering groups customers who behave alike.
e6548e18f3.wrong: No labels means unsupervised learning, so it's clustering. Linear and logistic regression both need a known target value to learn from.

21b7a179a2.question: A company uses a text-generation GenAI model for product descriptions, and the results are...
21b7a179a2.right: The output is steered purely by the text you give the model. That's prompt engineering; the model itself never changes.
21b7a179a2.wrong: It's prompt engineering: only the input text shapes the result. Model tuning would change the model's weights, which isn't happening here.

24c4372492.question: A developer is designing a function that should not unintentionally modify data outside it...
24c4372492.right: Immutable objects (ints, strings, tuples) can't be changed in place, so the function can't alter the caller's data.
24c4372492.wrong: Pass immutable objects. A function can change a mutable argument like a list or dict in place, and the caller will see that change.

c1c3638682.question: A programmer runs the following loop to display numbers: for i in range(3): print(i) What ...
c1c3638682.right: range(3) starts at 0 and stops before 3, giving 0, 1, 2.
c1c3638682.wrong: range(3) yields 0, 1, 2. It starts at 0 and the stop value 3 is never included.

2af991ee55.question: A Spark aggregation by city runs very slowly due to skew. What is the best solution?
2af991ee55.right: Salting adds a random suffix to hot keys so one heavy city is split across many tasks, then the partial results are combined.
2af991ee55.wrong: Use salting. Skew means a few keys hold most rows; a random salt on those keys spreads them out. More memory or a random repartition still sends each key to one task.

52843468fe.question: You are analyzing website traffic data over several months. You want to identify trends or...
52843468fe.right: Line charts plot values over time, which makes trends and seasonal cycles easy to spot.
52843468fe.wrong: A line chart shows change over time. Histograms and box plots show distributions, and pie charts show parts of a whole, so none of them show a trend.

1bbe4ea2df.question: A React component re-renders infinitely after an API call. What would be the root cause of...
1bbe4ea2df.right: If the effect sets state it also depends on (or has no dependency array), each update re-runs the fetch, forever.
1bbe4ea2df.wrong: The usual cause is a wrong useEffect dependency: the effect updates state that's also in its dependency list, so every render fetches again. A missing key only causes a warning.

0ae256ac4a.question: What is the output of for i in 1 2 3; do echo $i; done?
0ae256ac4a.right: echo adds a newline every time it runs, so 1, 2 and 3 land on separate lines.
0ae256ac4a.wrong: echo ends its output with a newline and runs once per value, so you get 1, 2 and 3 on three separate lines.

c43e9bf3a1.question: An email service automatically sorts messages into spam and non-spam categories. What type...
c43e9bf3a1.right: Spam or not-spam is a fixed set of labels, which makes it (binary) classification.
c43e9bf3a1.wrong: It's classification: each email gets one of two labels. Regression predicts a number, and clustering finds groups without labels.

208c594d2f.question: Main disadvantage of circuit switching:
208c594d2f.right: A circuit stays reserved for the whole call, even during silence, so that capacity sits idle.
208c594d2f.wrong: The weakness is wasted bandwidth: the circuit is held for the whole call even when nobody is talking. Voice quality on circuit-switched lines is actually good.

60986d2624.question: Which condition should replace the blank so that the list comprehension selects even value...
60986d2624.right: x % 2 is the remainder after dividing by 2, and it's 0 for even numbers.
60986d2624.wrong: Use x % 2 == 0, since even numbers leave no remainder. x < 0 matches nothing in range(5), and x == 0 keeps only 0.

a2cab2ae61.question: While exploring data types, you notice that a numeric column is stored as text. What type ...
a2cab2ae61.right: Numbers stored as text are a type inconsistency. Convert them (for example with pd.to_numeric) before doing any maths.
a2cab2ae61.wrong: It's a data type inconsistency: the values are numbers but the column type is text, so sums and comparisons break until you convert it.

1f26145ead.question: Which protocol is used for VoIP in packet networks?
1f26145ead.right: SIP (Session Initiation Protocol) sets up, manages and ends VoIP calls.
1f26145ead.wrong: It's SIP, which sets up and tears down VoIP calls. SS7, ISDN and TDM belong to the traditional circuit-switched phone network.

774876f472.question: You are running an async FastAPI application that works well during development but shows ...
774876f472.right: A blocking call (requests, time.sleep) inside async def freezes the event loop, so every request waits even though the CPU is idle.
774876f472.wrong: Low CPU with slow requests points to blocking I/O inside async code. It stalls the single event loop; use an async client or run the call in a thread pool.

e11223c745.question: Fault management primarily deals with:
e11223c745.right: Fault management is about detecting, logging and clearing alarms raised by network elements.
e11223c745.wrong: Fault management deals with alarms: detecting, correlating and clearing faults in the network. Coding, RF tuning and SIM making belong to other teams.

3e185c22c3.question: What differentiates Generative AI from traditional ML models?
3e185c22c3.right: Generative models produce new content (text, images, code) that resembles what they were trained on.
3e185c22c3.wrong: The difference is that GenAI creates new content. Traditional ML mostly predicts a label or a number; GenAI writes text, images or code.

40f429a2dc.question: A user prompts GenAI recent event response chatbot , but the chatbot provided unrelated re...
40f429a2dc.right: A confident but unrelated or made-up reply is a hallucination, which is common when the model lacks recent information.
40f429a2dc.wrong: This is hallucination: the reply isn't grounded in facts. Overfitting, underfitting and data leakage are training problems, not chatbot output problems.

b21956e957.question: What is the output of the following shell script?x="10"if [ $x -gt 5 ]; then echo "Yes"; e...
b21956e957.right: 10 -gt 5 is true, so the then branch prints Yes.
b21956e957.wrong: It prints Yes. -gt compares numbers, 10 is greater than 5, so the then branch runs.

3b22661af1.question: Which of the following is an example of supervised learning?
3b22661af1.right: Past sales give known prices, so the data is labeled. That makes it supervised learning (regression).
3b22661af1.wrong: Supervised learning needs labeled data, as in predicting house prices from past sales. Grouping customers and finding hidden patterns are unsupervised.

e2c7098481.question: A software application is running in a production environment where monitoring, debugging,...
e2c7098481.right: The logging module gives you levels, timestamps, handlers and formats, which production monitoring depends on.
e2c7098481.wrong: Use Python's logging module. print and plain stdout have no levels or timestamps, and a custom logger rebuilds what logging already does.

caa73688d4.question: What does the command below do?cat file.txt | wc -l
caa73688d4.right: wc -l counts lines, so this prints how many lines file.txt has.
caa73688d4.wrong: wc -l counts lines; cat just feeds the file in. Counting only matching lines would need grep -c.

7f54067933.question: When Form inputs behave inconsistently across renders. What would be the root cause?
7f54067933.right: An input that flips between controlled (value set) and uncontrolled (value undefined) behaves unpredictably, and React warns about it.
7f54067933.wrong: The cause is mixing controlled and uncontrolled inputs, often when value starts as undefined. Give state an initial value such as an empty string so the input stays controlled.

9f613e029b.question: You need to read data from a file in Python and make sure system resources are released pr...
9f613e029b.right: with open() closes the file automatically, even when an exception is raised.
9f613e029b.wrong: Use with open(). The context manager closes the file even after an error. try-finally also works but is longer and easier to get wrong.

2deeb34dc7.question: A developer is writing a function that adds two numbers and sends the result back to the c...
2deeb34dc7.right: return hands the value back to the caller, whereas print only shows it on screen.
2deeb34dc7.wrong: Use return a+b. print just displays the sum and the function still returns None; yield would turn it into a generator.

f4beead718.question: PSTN primarily uses which switching method?
f4beead718.right: The PSTN sets up a dedicated circuit for each call.
f4beead718.wrong: The PSTN uses circuit switching, a dedicated path per call. Packet switching is what the internet and VoIP use.

2f29fa43eb.question: If the key "key" is not present in the dictionary data, what should be used as the default...
2f29fa43eb.right: None is the usual way to say 'no value', and it's also what get() returns when you don't pass a default.
2f29fa43eb.wrong: The conventional default is None, which is also what get() returns if you leave the default out. KeyError is an exception, not a value.

12a58ff013.question: In LTE Which layer handles modulation and coding?
12a58ff013.right: The physical layer handles modulation, coding and the radio signal itself.
12a58ff013.wrong: Modulation and coding happen at PHY. MAC handles scheduling, RLC handles segmentation and retransmission, and RRC handles control signaling.

bdd8642542.question: While we are rendering 5,000 or more items there would be an UI lag. How can we optimize t...
bdd8642542.right: Virtualization renders only the rows on screen, and memo stops unchanged rows from re-rendering.
bdd8642542.wrong: Use memo plus virtualization (react-window, for example) so only visible rows are rendered. Redux or class components don't reduce the number of DOM nodes.

cafc034d55.question: A developer notices that a Spark job is taking longer than expected, even though the trans...
cafc034d55.right: Transformations only build a plan. The work runs at an action such as count() or collect(), so that's where the time shows up.
cafc034d55.wrong: Spark is lazy: transformations just record a plan, and everything runs at the first action. That's why the time appears there, not at the simple transformations.

8a00b76aeb.question: You are building a feature that needs to frequently check whether a value exists in a coll...
8a00b76aeb.right: Sets are hash-based, so a membership check is O(1) on average.
8a00b76aeb.wrong: Use a set. Its membership checks are O(1) on average thanks to hashing, while lists and tuples scan every element (O(n)).

854face2e5.question: A team wants testing activities to start parallel with development. Which SDLC model suppo...
854face2e5.right: The V-Model pairs every development phase with a test phase that is planned at the same time.
854face2e5.wrong: It's the V-Model, which pairs each development phase with a test phase. Waterfall leaves testing until the build is finished.

21eddcccd2.question: A developer wants to search for the word "error" inside a log file. Which command should b...
21eddcccd2.right: grep searches text inside files, for example grep "error" app.log.
21eddcccd2.wrong: Use grep to search inside a file. find and locate look for files by name, not for text inside them.

e3a24a65ee.question: A script needs to store temporary values only inside the script execution. Which variable ...
e3a24a65ee.right: A local variable exists only while the script or function runs and disappears afterwards.
e3a24a65ee.wrong: Use a local variable. Environment and exported variables get passed on to child processes, which temporary values don't need.

2704312d97.question: A developer wants to reuse a set of commands multiple times in a script. What should they ...
2704312d97.right: A function groups commands under a name, so you can call it as many times as you like.
2704312d97.wrong: Write a function: it bundles commands under a name you can call again. A loop repeats code in one spot but can't be called from elsewhere.

f92c5eb522.question: What does the following command do? cat file.txt
f92c5eb522.right: cat prints a file's contents to the terminal.
f92c5eb522.wrong: cat displays a file's contents. Deleting is rm, renaming is mv and copying is cp.

1f4daf8178.question: What is the output? name="Linux" echo "Hello $name"
1f4daf8178.right: Variables are expanded inside double quotes, so $name becomes Linux.
1f4daf8178.wrong: It prints Hello Linux because the shell expands $name inside double quotes. Single quotes would print $name literally.

6ec91f61e6.question: What will be the output? num=7 if [ $num -gt 5 ] then echo "Greater" else echo "Smaller" f...
6ec91f61e6.right: 7 -gt 5 is true, so it prints Greater.
6ec91f61e6.wrong: It prints Greater: 7 is greater than 5, so the then branch runs.

0744067709.question: Which command is used to list files in a directory?
0744067709.right: ls lists the contents of a directory.
0744067709.wrong: On Linux it's ls. dir is the Windows command, and list and show aren't standard commands.

cf8d26878b.question: Which symbol is used to define a variable in a shell script?
cf8d26878b.right: Assignment is name=value with no spaces. The $ is only for reading the value.
cf8d26878b.wrong: Write name=value, with no $ and no spaces around the =. The $ is only used to read a variable, as in echo $name.

5b711c6c26.question: Which SDLC model follows a sequential approach where each phase must be completed before t...
5b711c6c26.right: Waterfall runs each phase to completion before the next one starts.
5b711c6c26.wrong: That's Waterfall: requirements, design, build, test and deploy, each finished before the next. Agile and Spiral work in repeated cycles.

fb06d7397d.question: Which shell is the default shell in most Linux systems today?
fb06d7397d.right: Bash (the Bourne Again Shell) is the default on most Linux distributions.
fb06d7397d.wrong: Bash is the default on most Linux distributions. The Bourne shell came before it, and C shell and Korn shell are alternatives.

222a6bce5d.question: Which operator is used for numeric equality comparison in shell scripting?
222a6bce5d.wrong: Use -eq for numbers inside [ ]. = and == compare strings, and === doesn't exist in shell.

7300b5fe28.question: What will be printed? for i in 1 2 3 do echo $i done
7300b5fe28.right: The loop echoes 1, 2 and 3 in order, one per line.
7300b5fe28.wrong: The loop prints 1, then 2, then 3, each on its own line. 123 would need echo -n, and nothing reverses the order.

a26d1029be.question: Which special variable represents all arguments passed to a script as separate strings?
a26d1029be.right: "$@" expands to every argument as a separate word, so arguments containing spaces stay intact.
a26d1029be.wrong: It's $@: all arguments, each as a separate string. $1 is only the first argument, $# is the count and $? is the last exit status.

6ba6fe4e4c.question: Which command is used to display the current working directory?
6ba6fe4e4c.right: pwd stands for print working directory.
6ba6fe4e4c.wrong: Use pwd. ls lists files, cd changes directory and whoami prints your username.

e443ae36dc.question: A script should execute different blocks of code based on multiple values of a variable. W...
e443ae36dc.right: case matches one variable against many patterns, which is cleaner than a long if/elif chain.
e443ae36dc.wrong: Use case: it checks one variable against several values in one tidy block. if/elif works but gets messy with many values.

88699a3774.question: A developer wants to create a new directory called project_files. Which command should be ...
88699a3774.wrong: The command is mkdir project_files. create and newdir don't exist, and dir lists files.

0781134107.question: What is the primary goal of the Requirement Phase in SDLC?
0781134107.right: The requirements phase pins down what users need before any design or code begins.
0781134107.wrong: The requirements phase is about understanding what users need. Coding, testing and deployment come in later phases.

24e1040140.question: What will this script output? function greet(){ echo "Welcome" } greet
24e1040140.right: Calling greet runs the function body, which echoes Welcome.
24e1040140.wrong: It prints Welcome. The function is defined first and then called by name, which runs its echo.

214db607b4.question: A script should repeat an operation until a user enters "exit". Which loop is best suited?
214db607b4.right: A while loop keeps going while the input isn't exit, e.g. while [ "$input" != "exit" ].
214db607b4.wrong: The expected answer is a while loop that runs until the input is exit. An until loop can do it with the condition flipped, but while is the standard pick; for loops walk a known list.

745a4e60e9.question: What is the output? a=5 b=3 echo $((a+b))
745a4e60e9.wrong: It prints 8 because $(( )) does arithmetic. 53 would be string joining, which isn't what $(( )) does.

e716ad3394.question: A company wants to release software quickly in multiple iterations with customer feedback....
e716ad3394.right: Agile delivers in short iterations and folds customer feedback into each one.
e716ad3394.wrong: Agile fits: short iterations, frequent releases and feedback after each one. Waterfall and V-Model deliver once at the end.

bb607d51c6.question: A script should check whether a number is greater than 10. Which condition is correct?
bb607d51c6.right: Inside [ ], -gt is the numeric 'greater than' test.
bb607d51c6.wrong: Use -gt. Inside [ ], > is treated as output redirection and creates a file named 10; gt without the dash isn't an operator.

3fafcf15d0.question: A developer wants to redirect script output to a file. Which operator is used?
3fafcf15d0.right: > sends output to a file and overwrites it; >> appends instead.
3fafcf15d0.wrong: Use > to send output to a file (>> appends). < reads input from a file, | passes output to another command and & runs it in the background.

77e1160948.question: What does this script do? count=1 while [ $count -le 3 ] do echo $count ((count++)) done
77e1160948.right: count starts at 1, is printed, then incremented, and the loop stops once count passes 3.
77e1160948.wrong: It prints 1, 2, 3. ((count++)) raises count each pass, so the loop ends when count reaches 4 and the test -le 3 fails.

ce8fc9387d.question: numbers = [1,2,2,3,3,4] result = list(set(numbers)) print(result) Which statement is TRUE?
ce8fc9387d.right: A set removes duplicates but has no guaranteed order, so the list you get back may not keep the original order.
ce8fc9387d.wrong: A set removes duplicates but promises no order. Small ints often come out sorted in CPython, but that's an implementation detail you can't rely on.

fb1a3fa8e2.question: Why do scripts use if __name__ == "__main__":?
fb1a3fa8e2.right: __name__ is "__main__" only when the file is run directly, so the guarded code is skipped on import.
fb1a3fa8e2.wrong: The guard runs code only when the file is executed directly. When imported, __name__ is the module name, so that block is skipped. Files import fine without it.

89dbc1d072.question: Which import statement imports only the sqrt function from the math module?
89dbc1d072.right: from module import name brings in just that one name.
89dbc1d072.wrong: Use from math import sqrt. import math.sqrt fails because sqrt is a function, not a submodule.

27974ec3a8.question: A class Car already has a method named start(). Another class ElectricCar(Car) defines its...
27974ec3a8.right: A subclass redefining a parent method with the same name is method overriding.
27974ec3a8.wrong: It's method overriding: the subclass replaces the parent's start(). Overloading means same name with different parameters, which Python doesn't support directly.

3723ca029e.question: A project contains the following structure: project/ app.py utils.py Which statement impor...
3723ca029e.right: The module is named after the file (utils), and you import calculate from it.
3723ca029e.wrong: Use from utils import calculate. import utils.calculate fails because calculate is a function, not a submodule.

5bb511ff88.question: Assume the file sample.txt contains: Python AI Python file: with open("sample.txt") as fil...
5bb511ff88.right: readlines() reads to the end of the file, so the following readline() returns an empty string and prints a blank line.
5bb511ff88.wrong: It prints 2, then an empty line. readlines() already moved to the end of the file, so readline() has nothing left and returns ''.

03c67df6a5.question: Which OOP concept allows a child class to use methods from its parent class?
03c67df6a5.right: Inheritance lets a child class reuse the parent's methods without rewriting them.
03c67df6a5.wrong: That's inheritance: the child class gets the parent's methods for free. Polymorphism is about the same call behaving differently on different classes.

d9787bf726.question: A developer wants to reverse the string "Python". Which statement produces "nohtyP"?
d9787bf726.right: The slice [::-1] steps through the string backwards and returns a new string.
d9787bf726.wrong: Use name[::-1]. Strings have no reverse() or sort() method, and reversed() returns an iterator, not a string.

3ba2247226.question: A CSV file contains thousands of records. The developer wants to process one row at a time...
3ba2247226.right: csv.reader reads the file lazily, one row at a time, so memory stays flat.
3ba2247226.wrong: Use csv.reader(file), which yields one row at a time. read(), readlines() and list(file) all load the whole file into memory first.

dd04eea383.question: A package contains several modules. The developer wants to make the folder recognizable as...
dd04eea383.right: An __init__.py file marks a folder as a regular package. It's optional since Python 3.3 but still standard practice.
dd04eea383.wrong: The file is __init__.py. Older Python versions only treat a folder as a package if it has one; setup.py is for packaging and distribution.

4ee6ac26e3.question: A module contains reusable utility functions. Multiple projects need those functions. What...
4ee6ac26e3.right: One shared module means you write and fix the code once, and every project picks up the change.
4ee6ac26e3.wrong: The benefit is reuse and easier maintenance: one copy of the code to fix and test. Moving code into a module doesn't make it faster or use less memory.

26bcb8de26.question: Why is the following code considered a best practice? if __name__ == "__main__": main()
26bcb8de26.right: It keeps main() from running when the file is imported, so the module can be reused safely.
26bcb8de26.wrong: The guard makes main() run only when the file is executed directly, not on import. It has no effect on speed or syntax errors.

a74a9cf2cf.question: A program receives text with random capitalization. PYTHON programming The developer wants...
a74a9cf2cf.right: title() capitalises the first letter of every word and lowercases the rest.
a74a9cf2cf.wrong: Use title(), which gives Python Programming. capitalize() only capitalises the first word (Python programming), and upper() makes everything uppercase.

69ec35c693.question: In a for ... else loop, when does the else block run?
69ec35c693.right: The else on a loop runs only if the loop wasn't stopped by break, which makes it handy for 'not found' cases.
69ec35c693.wrong: A loop's else runs only when the loop finishes without a break. It also runs when the loop has zero iterations, but that isn't the only case.

65f92fc2ad.question: What will be the output? class Animal: def sound(self): return "Animal" class Dog(Animal):...
65f92fc2ad.right: Dog overrides sound(), so a returns Animal and b returns Bark.
65f92fc2ad.wrong: It prints Animal Bark. Each object uses its own class's method: Animal's for a, Dog's override for b.

0105fda0e8.question: You must check whether each of 1,00,000 incoming IDs already exists among 50,000 stored ID...
0105fda0e8.right: A set lookup is O(1) on average, so 100,000 checks stay fast.
0105fda0e8.wrong: Use a set. Each list or tuple lookup scans up to 50,000 items; a sorted list needs a binary search (O(log n)), while a set is O(1) on average.

618f605f8f.question: Which statement correctly converts a Python dictionary into a JSON string?
618f605f8f.right: json.dumps returns a string; the s stands for string.
618f605f8f.wrong: Use json.dumps(data). json.dump writes to a file object, and load/loads go the other way, from JSON back to Python.

d6362e01e4.question: Which string method removes leading and trailing whitespace?
d6362e01e4.right: strip() removes whitespace from both ends; lstrip() and rstrip() do one side each.
d6362e01e4.wrong: Python uses strip(). trim() is the JavaScript name, and remove() and clean() aren't string methods.

90f6b73d2f.question: Which statement correctly creates a dictionary with employee IDs as keys and names as valu...
90f6b73d2f.right: Curly braces with key: value pairs create a dictionary.
90f6b73d2f.wrong: Dictionaries use curly braces: {101: "John", 102: "Mary"}. Square brackets and parentheses with colons are syntax errors.

8fcddc59cf.question: Which of the following is used to add a new element to the end of a Python list?
8fcddc59cf.right: append() adds a single item to the end of a list.
8fcddc59cf.wrong: Use append(). insert() needs a position, extend() adds every item from another iterable, and add() is for sets.

eb7b0383b7.question: Which statement about Python sets is TRUE?
eb7b0383b7.right: A set keeps only one copy of each value, so duplicates disappear automatically.
eb7b0383b7.wrong: Sets automatically drop duplicates. They aren't indexable, they don't keep insertion order, and they can hold any hashable type.

6241ee073f.question: Which of the following is a valid Python variable name?
6241ee073f.right: Names can contain letters, digits and underscores, but can't start with a digit or be a keyword.
6241ee073f.wrong: user_name is valid. 2user starts with a digit, user-name contains a minus sign, and class is a reserved keyword.

eca8fd1ffa.question: What is the output of the following code? print(10 // 3)
eca8fd1ffa.right: // is floor division, so 10 // 3 drops the remainder and gives 3.
eca8fd1ffa.wrong: // is floor division: 10 // 3 is 3. 3.33 would come from /, and 1 is the remainder you'd get from %.

e0217b9f4e.question: Which file mode allows reading and writing without deleting existing file content?
e0217b9f4e.right: r+ opens an existing file for reading and writing without truncating it.
e0217b9f4e.wrong: Use r+. w and w+ empty the file as soon as it opens, and a only lets you write at the end.

baa8cfa919.question: import json data = {"name":"Alex"} text = json.dumps(data) obj = json.loads(text) print(ty...
baa8cfa919.right: json.loads turns the JSON string back into a Python dict.
baa8cfa919.wrong: It's a dict. dumps turns the dict into a string, and loads parses that string back into a dict.

94cedcae88.question: What is the output of the following FastAPI code? @app.get('/hello') def hello(): return {...
94cedcae88.right: FastAPI serialises the returned dict to JSON and sets the Content-Type header for you.
94cedcae88.wrong: The client gets JSON. FastAPI converts the returned dict into a JSON response; clients never receive Python objects directly.

97485c4811.question: Consider the Node.js code: const fs = require('fs'); fs.readFile('data.txt','utf8',(err,da...
97485c4811.right: readFile is asynchronous, so console.log('Done') runs first and the callback fires later.
97485c4811.wrong: Done prints first. readFile doesn't block; its callback runs once the file has been read, after the synchronous code has finished.

85309a128a.question: A web application makes several API calls one after another, even though they are independ...
85309a128a.right: Promise.all starts all the requests at once, so the total wait is about as long as the slowest call.
85309a128a.wrong: Run them concurrently with Promise.all(). Independent calls don't need to wait for each other, so total time drops to roughly the slowest single call.

61fb6bbfb5.question: What is the output of the following code? async function test(){ return 100; } test().then...

7e0e65757d.wrong: Use resource tags, such as env and costcenter labels, for governance and cost reports. DNS records and zones have nothing to do with grouping.

36c3d54a0c.right: Deleting a resource group deletes every resource inside it, which is why resource locks exist.

240bcacd45.right: Queue Storage holds messages so producers and workers can run independently and at different speeds.
240bcacd45.wrong: Use Azure Queue Storage for simple message queues. Blob Storage and Files store files, and DNS resolves names.

9992343b68.wrong: Use Azure Table Storage. SQL Database is relational, Files is file shares, and a Load Balancer distributes traffic.

b2b15506d5.wrong: Run tests before the production deployment stage. Testing after deploying means broken code is already live.

be36ce0e97.right: Data residency rules decide which regions you're allowed to store and process data in.
be36ce0e97.wrong: Region selection is directly affected. Data residency laws limit where data can be stored, which means choosing regions inside that boundary.

4f0446ca49.question: A storage workload consists of millions of images accessed as objects over HTTPS. Which Az...

4f0446ca49.wrong: Use Blob Storage for objects served over HTTPS. Azure Files is mounted as a file share, and Queue Storage holds messages.

c2a6e61ee4.question: A cloud application needs redundancy against a regional disaster, not merely a single-zone...
c2a6e61ee4.right: Zones protect against one datacenter failing. Surviving a whole-region outage needs multi-region deployment or disaster recovery.
c2a6e61ee4.wrong: Look at a multi-region or disaster-recovery setup. Bigger disks or more VMs in the same zone can't survive a whole region going down.

a5b716e9a7.question: A developer needs to manage resources in one production resource group but must not modify...
a5b716e9a7.right: Scoping the role to that one resource group gives exactly the access needed and nothing else (least privilege).
a5b716e9a7.wrong: Assign the role at the production resource group's scope. Subscription Owner or Global Administrator would also give access to the other group.

1a1716dac8.question: A deployment template creates resources with dependencies. One resource must exist before ...
1a1716dac8.right: Templates declare dependencies (dependsOn or references), so Azure creates resources in the right order.
1a1716dac8.wrong: Use declared dependencies or references in the template, such as dependsOn in ARM. DNS TTL and storage tiers have nothing to do with deployment order.

e2e66f78bd.question: A regulated organization requires a cloud environment dedicated to its own organizational ...
e2e66f78bd.right: A private cloud is dedicated to one organisation, which suits strict regulatory control.
e2e66f78bd.wrong: That's a private cloud: infrastructure dedicated to one organisation. Public cloud is shared, and hybrid mixes on-premises with public.

b6d679c3be.question: An application must tolerate failure of a single Azure datacenter facility while remaining...
b6d679c3be.right: Redundant instances in several zones survive the loss of one datacenter without leaving the region.
b6d679c3be.wrong: Deploy redundant instances across availability zones. A bigger VM or everything in one zone still fails with that datacenter.

296ad7540d.question: A business application requires relational transactions, SQL queries, constraints, and man...
296ad7540d.right: Azure SQL Database gives you relational tables, transactions and constraints as a managed service.
296ad7540d.wrong: Use Azure SQL Database for relational data and transactions. Queue and Blob Storage don't support SQL queries or constraints, and CDN caches content.

3c840b8e42.question: A company needs to audit who created, deleted, or modified Azure resources. Which Azure ca...
3c840b8e42.right: The Activity Log records control-plane operations: who created, changed or deleted which resource, and when.
3c840b8e42.wrong: Use the Azure Activity Log. It records who created, modified or deleted resources. The other options don't track control-plane changes.

bdb78380a4.question: A company wants Azure to provide physical infrastructure while multiple customers use logi...
bdb78380a4.right: In public cloud the provider owns the hardware and many customers share it, isolated logically.
bdb78380a4.wrong: That's public cloud: shared provider-owned infrastructure with logical isolation between customers. Private cloud and single-tenant setups serve one organisation.

ef8c6d5fa1.question: An application needs to retrieve secrets from Azure without embedding a client secret in i...
ef8c6d5fa1.right: The app authenticates with its managed identity and reads secrets from Key Vault, so no client secret lives in the code.
ef8c6d5fa1.wrong: Use a managed identity with Key Vault. Azure supplies the identity's credentials, so there's nothing to embed. Public blob access would expose secrets instead.

ff658c6acf.question: An application deployed in one Azure region has high latency for users on another continen...
ff658c6acf.right: Distance adds latency, so the first thing to check is where compute and data sit relative to users. Extra regions or a CDN help.
ff658c6acf.wrong: Check where compute and data are placed relative to users. Users on another continent pay for the round-trip distance; tags and names don't affect speed.

c4c3211832.question: A team wants infrastructure changes to be reviewable, versioned, and reproducible before d...
c4c3211832.right: Infrastructure as Code in Git gets pull-request review, history and repeatable automated deploys.
c4c3211832.wrong: Keep declarative infrastructure definitions in version control and deploy them through a pipeline. Manual portal changes can't be reviewed or reproduced.

2d145930ae.question: A storage account contains confidential documents. The security requirement is to prevent ...
2d145930ae.right: Turning off anonymous access and requiring authenticated, authorised requests keeps confidential blobs private.
2d145930ae.wrong: Disable or restrict public access and require authentication (Entra ID or SAS). Enabling public container access is the exact opposite of what's needed.

b04362571e.question: A company migrates an existing application to Azure but requires OS-level control because ...
b04362571e.right: Only IaaS (a VM) gives you control of the OS and kernel, which a custom kernel module needs.
b04362571e.wrong: It has to be IaaS. A custom kernel module needs OS-level control, which PaaS and SaaS deliberately hide from you.

c5be2f9181.question: A smaller Linear Regression error generally indicates that:
c5be2f9181.right: Regression error (such as MSE or MAE) measures how far predictions are from the true values, so smaller means closer.
c5be2f9181.wrong: Smaller error means the predicted values are closer to the actual targets. Counting correctly classified examples is a classification metric, not regression.

2fbca518de.question: A company uses KNN to predict whether a customer will purchase a product. One feature is "...
2fbca518de.right: KNN uses distances, so a feature measured in hundreds of thousands drowns out one that ranges from 1 to 50. Scale the features first.
2fbca518de.wrong: Income's huge scale dominates the distance calculation. KNN handles numbers fine; standardise or normalise the features so each one counts.

5140c41492.question: A KNN classifier gives excellent accuracy on the training dataset but performs poorly on u...
5140c41492.right: With K=1 each prediction copies the single closest training point, noise included, which is classic overfitting.
5140c41492.wrong: K=1 overfits: it memorises every training point, noise included. Training accuracy is perfect, but it doesn't generalise. Underfitting comes from a very large K.

f7bbbf1e40.question: A team compares a Linear Regression model, KNN, and K-Means for predicting the future sale...
f7bbbf1e40.right: K-Means only groups data. It has no target to predict, so it can't be compared with regression on sales amounts.
f7bbbf1e40.wrong: K-Means is unsupervised and doesn't predict a target value, so it doesn't belong in a sales-prediction comparison. Linear Regression (and KNN regression) can predict numbers.

68aea8e6f7.question: A sentence contains the words "The animal didn't cross the road because it was injured." T...
68aea8e6f7.right: Attention lets the representation of "it" draw more heavily from "animal", which is how the model resolves the reference.
68aea8e6f7.wrong: Attention gives more weight to the relevant context words, here "animal", when building the representation of "it". Equal weights would lose that link.

e84417cc5a.question: A developer increases the number of attention heads in a Transformer and notices that the ...
e84417cc5a.right: Each head has its own learned projections, so one might track syntax while another tracks references.
e84417cc5a.wrong: Different heads learn different relationships, such as grammar in one and references in another. They aren't separate models and don't replace feed-forward layers.

29f47ef430.question: What generally happens when the value of K in KNN is increased substantially?
29f47ef430.right: A larger K averages over more neighbours, so single noisy points matter less (too large and it underfits).
29f47ef430.wrong: A larger K looks at a bigger neighbourhood, so predictions become smoother and less sensitive to individual points. KNN still uses distances.

93e0fa920b.question: What is the primary purpose of the attention mechanism in a Transformer?
93e0fa920b.right: Attention scores how much each token should draw on every other token when building its contextual meaning.
93e0fa920b.wrong: Attention decides how strongly each token relates to the others when building its representation. It doesn't remove tokens or replace embeddings.

d0f1789ed2.question: A Transformer model has learned strong relationships between words but produces poor resul...
d0f1789ed2.right: Self-attention has no built-in sense of order, so positional encodings are added to the token embeddings.
d0f1789ed2.wrong: Add positional information, i.e. positional encodings. On its own, self-attention treats the input as an unordered set of tokens.

f59a0f7cb8.question: A Transformer receives a long document and must determine which earlier sentence is releva...
f59a0f7cb8.right: Every token can attend directly to any earlier token in the context, however far back it is.
f59a0f7cb8.wrong: Self-attention links the current token directly to relevant tokens anywhere in the context. It doesn't give equal importance or delete tokens.

57d0c606aa.question: A Transformer processes the sentence "I went to the bank to deposit money." Why might the ...
57d0c606aa.right: The vector for bank is built with attention to its neighbours (deposit, money vs river), so it changes with context.
57d0c606aa.wrong: Attention mixes in surrounding context, so bank near "deposit money" gets a different representation than bank near "river". The token itself is the same.

4a09e42f0e.question: In K-Means clustering, what does the centroid represent?
4a09e42f0e.right: A centroid is the mean of all points in its cluster, the cluster's centre.
4a09e42f0e.wrong: The centroid is the mean position of the points assigned to the cluster. It's usually not an actual data point, and it isn't a class label.

172d973176.question: A data scientist chooses K=3 for K-Means and observes that several unrelated groups of cus...
172d973176.right: K is a guess until tested. The elbow method or silhouette scores help pick a better one.
172d973176.wrong: Try different values of K and compare them, for example with the elbow method or silhouette score. K-Means has no learning rate, and dropping features blindly isn't a fix.

9ea8eefb8b.question: Which distance measure is commonly used to determine similarity between a data point and a...
9ea8eefb8b.right: Standard K-Means assigns each point to the nearest centroid by Euclidean distance.
9ea8eefb8b.wrong: Standard K-Means uses Euclidean distance. Cosine, Hamming and Jaccard are used in other settings, such as text or binary data.

cfc75a44b3.question: KNN makes a prediction primarily by:
cfc75a44b3.right: KNN has no real training step. At prediction time it finds the closest examples and votes or averages their labels.
cfc75a44b3.wrong: KNN looks at the nearest training examples and uses their labels (a vote) or values (an average). It doesn't learn an equation or build centroids.

012bea44a9.question: A KNN model achieves poor performance even after increasing K. Inspection shows that one f...
012bea44a9.right: No K can fix a distorted distance. Scale the features first, then tune K.
012bea44a9.wrong: The feature scale is distorting distances, so fix the preprocessing (scaling) before tuning K. Changing K doesn't change how distances are calculated.

0feedfc437.question: A dataset contains house sizes and corresponding prices. After training Linear Regression,...
0feedfc437.right: A consistent miss at one end of the range means a straight line doesn't fit the true curve well.
0feedfc437.wrong: A systematic error for large houses suggests the relationship isn't linear across the whole range. Try polynomial features, a log transform or a non-linear model.

6f74b897eb.question: A team feeds the sentence "The bank approved the loan" into an embedding model. The result...
6f74b897eb.right: A sentence embedding captures meaning, so it lands near related text and far from unrelated text.
6f74b897eb.wrong: An embedding should capture semantic meaning, which lets you tell this sentence apart from unrelated text. It isn't a character count or a single label.

f504228def.question: A K-Means model is trained on customer data containing annual income and spending score. I...
f504228def.right: Standardising both features puts them on a comparable scale, so spending score can shape the clusters too.
f504228def.wrong: Scale the features, for example with StandardScaler. Income's big range dominates Euclidean distance; more iterations or dropping a feature won't fix that.

442b503fbe.question: In Linear Regression, the model attempts to learn:
442b503fbe.right: Linear Regression fits weights linking the features to a continuous number.
442b503fbe.wrong: Linear Regression learns a relationship between features and a continuous target. Clusters belong to K-Means, and nearest examples belong to KNN.

04462e314f.question: In a Transformer, embeddings are mainly used to:
04462e314f.right: Embeddings turn token IDs into dense vectors where similar meanings sit close together.
04462e314f.wrong: Embeddings represent tokens as numerical vectors that carry meaning. Attention then works on those vectors; it isn't replaced by them.

958b22bf70.question: Which statement best describes the main advantage of Transformers over traditional sequent...
958b22bf70.right: Attention looks at all token pairs at once, so training runs in parallel instead of step by step as in an RNN.
958b22bf70.wrong: The big advantage is parallelism: attention relates all tokens at once instead of one step at a time. Transformers still need numbers and data, and they're often larger.

3cd6cf7ba4.question: A regression model predicts house prices using only house area. The residual plot shows a ...
3cd6cf7ba4.right: Residuals should scatter randomly around zero. A curved pattern means the straight line is missing a non-linear trend.
3cd6cf7ba4.wrong: A curved residual pattern shows the linear model is missing a non-linear relationship. A good fit leaves random scatter around zero.

c3ae26b538.question: Why are Q, K, and V vectors used in self-attention?
c3ae26b538.right: The query is what a token looks for, keys are what others offer to match, and values are the information that gets mixed in.
c3ae26b538.wrong: Q is what a token is looking for, K is what each token offers for matching, and V is the content that gets combined. They have nothing to do with dataset splits.

d763ac2acb.question: A K-Means system is run twice on the same dataset with the same K, but produces different ...
d763ac2acb.right: K-Means only finds a local optimum, so different starting centroids can end in different clusters. Fix the random seed or use k-means++.
d763ac2acb.wrong: Random starting centroids can lead to different local solutions. K stays fixed, and the distance metric doesn't change. Set a seed or use k-means++ with several runs.

e4b596910d.question: import numpy as np a = np.array([[1], [2], [3]]) b = np.array([10, 20]) print(a + b) What ...
e4b596910d.right: Shape (3,1) plus shape (2,) broadcasts to (3,2): each row value is added to both 10 and 20.
e4b596910d.wrong: It's [[11, 21], [12, 22], [13, 23]]. Broadcasting stretches the (3,1) column and the (2,) row into a (3,2) grid, so there's no error.

ce4716014c.question: A large CSV contains 20 million rows and cannot comfortably fit into memory. Which Pandas ...
ce4716014c.right: read_csv(chunksize=...) streams the file, so you aggregate each chunk and combine the partial results.
ce4716014c.wrong: Read the file in chunks (read_csv with chunksize) and combine partial aggregates, such as sums and counts for a mean. Loading all 20 million rows at once is the problem.

470a3e197d.question: A Pandas DataFrame joins transactions to customer metadata. Customer ID is duplicated in t...
470a3e197d.right: Check that the key is really unique first (e.g. merge with validate="many_to_one"), otherwise duplicates multiply rows silently.
470a3e197d.wrong: Validate the key's uniqueness and fix the duplicate customers before joining. Duplicate keys in the lookup table are why the transaction rows multiplied.

60f4dbfcc1.question: Two vectors are `[1, 2, 3]` and `[2, 4, 6]`. Under cosine similarity, what relationship sh...
60f4dbfcc1.right: [2,4,6] is exactly twice [1,2,3], same direction, so the cosine similarity is 1.
60f4dbfcc1.wrong: Their cosine similarity is 1. Cosine only measures direction, and [2,4,6] points the same way as [1,2,3]; the difference in length is ignored.

100a6042fc.question: A 10,000-token document must be supplied to a model with a 4,000-token context window. The...
100a6042fc.right: 4,000 total minus 500 for the prompt leaves about 3,500 tokens for retrieved context.
100a6042fc.wrong: About 3,500 tokens: the 4,000-token window minus the 500-token prompt. In practice also reserve room for the model's answer.

1e89a79523.question: A retrieval corpus contains documents in two versions. Old chunks and current chunks have ...
1e89a79523.right: Version metadata on each chunk lets you filter to the current version even when the text is identical.
1e89a79523.wrong: Store document version metadata with each chunk and filter on it. Identical text means only metadata can tell old chunks from current ones.

2b6c68b541.question: A RAG application retrieves relevant chunks from several documents but provides no source ...
2b6c68b541.right: Keep source metadata with each chunk through retrieval so the answer can cite exactly where it came from.
2b6c68b541.wrong: Carry source and document metadata through retrieval and show citations in the answer. Bigger embeddings or random ordering don't make answers traceable.

46201cbed3.question: A GenAI pipeline logs `API_KEY=...` whenever an embedding request fails. What is the corre...
46201cbed3.right: Remove the secret from logs and rotate the key, since anyone who saw the logs could have copied it.
46201cbed3.wrong: Redact secrets from logs and rotate the exposed key. Base64 isn't encryption, and longer retention keeps the leak around longer.

616da23cb2.question: A keyword retriever scores a chunk by raw count of query-term occurrences. A chunk repeats...
616da23cb2.right: Capping or normalising term frequency (as BM25 does) stops repeated text from gaming the score.
616da23cb2.wrong: Use normalised or capped term frequency, as BM25 does, and judge relevance beyond repetition. Raw counts reward spam that repeats words.

c923824d68.question: A unit test for a text chunking function unexpectedly calls a real embedding API and becom...
c923824d68.right: Mocking or injecting the embedding client keeps the unit test fast and deterministic, and focused only on chunking.
c923824d68.wrong: Mock or inject the embedding dependency. A unit test should check chunking alone, not hit a real API that is slow and changes its output.

0914f1a136.question: A DataFrame contains `amount` values such as `"1200.50"`, `"N/A"`, and `"unknown"`. The pi...
0914f1a136.right: pd.to_numeric(errors="coerce") turns N/A and unknown into NaN, which median() skips, but decide explicitly how to handle them.
0914f1a136.wrong: Coerce to numbers (pd.to_numeric with errors="coerce") and handle the invalid values deliberately. The median of strings has no numeric meaning.

fda1354045.question: A data-quality rule says the batch must fail if more than 20% of documents cannot be parse...
fda1354045.right: Counting failures and failing only when the ratio passes 20% matches the rule exactly.
fda1354045.wrong: Track failures, compute the failure ratio, and fail the batch only when it exceeds 20%. Stopping at the first failure is stricter than the rule.

761775596d.question: Two normalized embedding vectors are `[0.6, 0.8]` and `[0.8, 0.6]`. What is their cosine s...
761775596d.right: For normalised vectors cosine similarity is the dot product: 0.6×0.8 + 0.8×0.6 = 0.96.
761775596d.wrong: It's 0.96. Both vectors have length 1, so cosine equals the dot product: 0.48 + 0.48. 0.48 is only half of that sum.

b3ef15d80c.question: A function accepts configuration and directly accesses `config['chunk_size']`. Missing con...
b3ef15d80c.right: Checking config at startup fails fast with a clear message, instead of a confusing KeyError deep in the pipeline.
b3ef15d80c.wrong: Validate required config at the entry point and raise a clear configuration error. Suppressing KeyErrors or using random defaults hides the real problem.

8d4ddaa719.question: A document contains 2,500 tokens. The chunk size is 600 tokens and the overlap is 100 toke...
8d4ddaa719.right: Chunks start at 0, 500, 1000, 1500 and 2000. The fifth one reaches the end at 2500.

844167998c.question: A retrieval system returns highly relevant chunks, but the generated answer frequently ign...
844167998c.right: Good retrieval plus bad answers points at the generation step, so evaluate them separately (faithfulness, grounding).
844167998c.wrong: Retrieval is fine, so the problem is in generation or how the context is used, which needs its own evaluation. Nothing suggests a corrupt index or zero vectors.

abc2fb2774.question: left = pd.DataFrame({ "id": [1, 2], "name": ["A", "B"] }) right = pd.DataFrame({ "id": [1,...
abc2fb2774.right: An inner merge pairs each left row with every matching right row: id 1 matches two rows and id 2 matches one, giving 3.
