e5497cf127.question: A Python module executes the entire document-ingestion pipeline as soon as another module ...
e5497cf127.right: Wrapping the pipeline in a function behind the __main__ guard means importing the module never starts ingestion.
e5497cf127.wrong: Put the pipeline in functions and call them only under if __name__ == '__main__':. Module-level code runs on every import.

9f21b9ef8d.question: A custom exception represents invalid user configuration, while a database timeout represe...
9f21b9ef8d.right: Separate types let callers catch each one differently: show a config error to the user, retry and alert on the timeout.
9f21b9ef8d.wrong: Different types let callers handle each case differently, such as retrying a timeout but reporting bad config to the user. They don't change speed or logging.

f5f06b6a51.question: A pipeline derives daily metrics from timestamps arriving in UTC, IST, and EST. Grouping d...
f5f06b6a51.right: Convert every timestamp to one reference timezone first; only then is 'the date' consistent.
f5f06b6a51.wrong: Normalise all timestamps to one reference timezone (often UTC) before deriving the date. Mixed zones put the same moment on different days.

68056ae56d.question: A chunk is 800 tokens, while the model's remaining context budget after system instruction...
68056ae56d.right: The whole prompt must fit the window, so trim, re-chunk or pick smaller pieces to stay within the 650 tokens left.
68056ae56d.wrong: Retrieve less, truncate or re-chunk so the prompt fits the 650 tokens left. The context limit is fixed; anything over it gets cut off or rejected.

67b1dd1c2d.question: A NumPy array `x` has shape `(100,1)` and `y` has shape `(1,50)`. What is the shape of `x ...
67b1dd1c2d.right: (100,1) and (1,50) both stretch along their size-1 axes, giving (100,50).
67b1dd1c2d.wrong: The result is (100, 50). Each size-1 dimension stretches to match the other array, so the column and the row form a full grid.

04ca5f724b.question: A dataset has a feature with 45% missing values. Replacing all missing values with zero ch...
04ca5f724b.right: Why values are missing, what the feature means, and how the model will use it all decide the right imputation.
04ca5f724b.wrong: Look at why the data is missing, what the feature means and how imputation affects the model. Zero-filling 45% of a column badly skews its distribution.

ed0a91247b.question: A simulated embedding function averages token vectors. A document contains no recognized t...
ed0a91247b.right: An empty token list would mean dividing by zero, so handle it explicitly: skip, flag or log the document.
ed0a91247b.wrong: Handle the empty case explicitly. Averaging zero vectors divides by zero, and a silent random vector corrupts search results.

24d82a060b.question: A RAG system stores embeddings but not source text or document metadata. Retrieval returns...
24d82a060b.right: Retrieval needs to return text the model can read, plus metadata for citations and filtering.
24d82a060b.wrong: Store the chunk text and stable source metadata with each vector. A vector ID alone gives the model nothing it can read.

066f694c68.question: A NumPy array has shape `(1000, 20)` and contains 1,000 observations with 20 features. The...
066f694c68.right: axis=0 collapses the rows (observations), leaving one mean per column: 20 values.
066f694c68.wrong: Use axis=0, which aggregates down the rows and gives 20 feature means. axis=1 would give 1,000 per-row means, and there is no axis 2 in a 2-D array.

39711d7866.question: A Python data pipeline processes each document independently. One malformed document shoul...
39711d7866.right: A try/except around each document logs the bad one and lets the loop carry on.
39711d7866.wrong: Put the try/except around each document's processing, log the failure and continue. Wrapping the whole batch stops everything at the first bad file.

6da2752a25.question: A data-cleaning function mutates a DataFrame supplied by its caller. Another component une...
6da2752a25.right: DataFrames are mutable and passed by reference, so in-place changes are visible to everyone holding the same object.
6da2752a25.wrong: The function mutates a shared, mutable object. Python passes a reference, not a copy, so return a modified copy or document that it mutates.

8ef39973a4.question: A RAG ingestion pipeline processes 20,000 documents. Re-running ingestion currently recomp...
8ef39973a4.right: Stable IDs plus content hashes show which documents changed, so only those are re-embedded.
8ef39973a4.wrong: Track stable document IDs and content hashes, and re-embed only what changed. Random IDs or wiping the index force everything to be redone.

a0414bedd5.question: A Pandas filter needs rows where `score >= 0.8` AND `status == 'approved'`. Which implemen...
a0414bedd5.right: Pandas needs element-wise & with each condition in parentheses: (df.score >= 0.8) & (df.status == 'approved').
a0414bedd5.wrong: Use & between parenthesised boolean Series. Python's and tries to get one True/False from a whole Series and raises a ValueError.

80f6792338.question: A tokenized sentence is represented as a matrix where each row is a token vector. The appl...
80f6792338.right: Rows are tokens, so axis=0 averages down the rows and gives one vector with the embedding's width.
80f6792338.wrong: Use np.mean(array, axis=0). It averages across the token rows and keeps every vector dimension; axis=1 would give one number per token instead.

93600f323e.question: A keyword retriever ranks documents by counting matching query terms. What problem can occ...
93600f323e.right: Raw counts reward length and repetition, so long or spammy documents rank too high.
93600f323e.wrong: Long or repetitive documents get inflated scores, because more words means more matches. Normalising by length (as BM25 does) fixes this.

47be92996a.question: A customer reference DataFrame contains duplicate customer IDs before it is joined to a tr...
47be92996a.right: If the key isn't unique, the join duplicates transaction rows, so check uniqueness before anything else.
47be92996a.wrong: Check whether the customer key is unique. Duplicate keys in the reference table multiply the joined rows; formatting and column order don't matter.

98e9505850.question: A NumPy array has shape (5, 3), where rows represent documents and columns represent featu...
98e9505850.right: axis=0 collapses the rows, so you get one result per feature column, computed across all documents.
98e9505850.wrong: axis=0 reduces down the document rows, giving one value per feature. Reducing across the feature columns of each document would be axis=1.

2e0be314f9.question: An AI application needs a named error specifically for an unsupported document format. Whi...
2e0be314f9.right: A custom exception names a specific failure (UnsupportedFormatError) so callers can catch and handle exactly that case.
2e0be314f9.wrong: A custom exception is a named error type for one specific condition. It doesn't replace logging, and it has nothing to do with speed or storing data.

3105b04c27.question: A retrieved RAG chunk is too large to fit within the model’s remaining context budget. Wha...
3105b04c27.right: Shrink or re-chunk the context so the whole prompt fits. Anything past the limit is cut or rejected.
3105b04c27.wrong: Reduce or re-chunk the retrieved text before generating. Sending it anyway overflows the context, and deleting the user's query defeats the purpose.

11d7a1c5e1.question: A text-cleaning function should remove leading and trailing spaces. Which assertion direct...
11d7a1c5e1.right: The assertion checks the exact expected output: both outer spaces gone, leaving 'text'.
11d7a1c5e1.wrong: Assert clean(' text ') == 'text'. That checks the exact result: leading and trailing spaces removed and the word kept.

84714dac6e.question: A RAG index stores embedding vectors and numeric IDs. Retrieval returns the IDs, but the a...
84714dac6e.right: Vector IDs alone are meaningless to the LLM. You need the chunk text (and source info) to build the prompt.
84714dac6e.wrong: The chunk text and its source metadata are missing. Retrieval gives IDs, but the model needs actual text to read and sources to cite.

cbd17f6edf.question: A BaseAgent class defines run(), while several specialized agents provide their own implem...
cbd17f6edf.right: Calling agent.run() works on any agent, and each subclass runs its own version. That's polymorphism.
cbd17f6edf.wrong: It's polymorphism: one run() interface with a different implementation in each agent. Inheritance doesn't force identical logic; overriding is what lets them differ.

622e5fde26.question: An AI application reads configuration settings before starting document processing. Why is...
622e5fde26.right: Keeping config separate from processing gives each part one job, which makes both easier to change and test.
622e5fde26.wrong: It improves separation of concerns. It doesn't validate every input or prevent exceptions; it just keeps two responsibilities apart.

cc99ca159d.question: A developer is investigating why an AI pipeline produces an unexpected embedding during de...
cc99ca159d.right: DEBUG is the most detailed level and is meant for diagnosing problems during development.
cc99ca159d.wrong: Use DEBUG for detailed diagnostic output. ERROR and CRITICAL are for failures and record less detail, and OFF records nothing.

f190a30b07.question: A keyword-based retriever should treat the terms AI, Ai, and ai as equivalent during match...
f190a30b07.right: Lowercasing makes AI, Ai and ai the same token, so letter case no longer affects matching.
f190a30b07.wrong: The goal is to remove differences caused by letter case. Lowercasing doesn't create embeddings and it deliberately throws away the original capitalisation.

177f60bba5.question: A unit test for a chunking function calls a live external API every time it runs. Why is t...
177f60bba5.right: Network calls are slow and their responses can change, so the test becomes slow and flaky.
177f60bba5.wrong: It makes the test slower and non-deterministic, since results depend on the network and the API. The chunking can still be tested; mock the API instead.

98aca9bfc5.question: During testing, an API token accidentally appears in an application log. What should the l...
98aca9bfc5.right: Redact the token before writing the log, e.g. replace it with ***. Logs are often widely readable.
98aca9bfc5.wrong: Redact the sensitive value before logging. Base64 is trivially reversible, and repeating the token or logging more just spreads the leak.

4c45c3db1f.question: A large CSV file is too large to load comfortably into memory as one DataFrame. Which Pand...
4c45c3db1f.right: pd.read_csv(..., chunksize=N) gives you manageable pieces you can process one at a time.
4c45c3db1f.wrong: Read the CSV in chunks with chunksize. Loading it repeatedly or converting rows to JSON only adds memory and work.

97b74d7e33.question: A RAG system compares two normalized embedding vectors that point in exactly the same dire...
97b74d7e33.right: Vectors pointing the same way have an angle of 0, and cos(0) = 1.
97b74d7e33.wrong: It should be 1. Cosine similarity measures the angle; same direction means angle 0 and cos 0 = 1. -1 is opposite and 0 is unrelated (orthogonal).

3e8174b507.question: A reusable AI pipeline contains several repeated processing steps. Which practice most dir...
3e8174b507.right: Small single-purpose functions are easy to read, reuse and test, and remove duplicated steps.
3e8174b507.wrong: Use small functions with clear responsibilities. One giant function, global config and copy-pasted logic all make the pipeline harder to change.

5debc11d8c.question: A retrieval system removes common stopwords from every document and query. Why might this ...
5debc11d8c.right: Words like 'not', 'without' or 'to be or not to be' can change meaning entirely, so dropping them can hurt.
5debc11d8c.wrong: Some stopwords carry meaning, like 'not' in 'not refundable'. Removing them blindly can flip what a query is asking.

3c7e446d45.question: A Pandas column contains the values '10', '25', and 'unknown'. Before calculating a numeri...
3c7e446d45.right: pd.to_numeric(errors='coerce') turns 'unknown' into NaN, and mean() skips NaN by default.
3c7e446d45.wrong: Use pd.to_numeric with errors='coerce'. Non-numbers become NaN and are skipped by mean(); sorting or concatenating strings gives no average.

7808d71eb2.question: A developer writes a text-cleaning function that should remove extra spaces. What is the m...
7808d71eb2.right: A unit test checks one behaviour of one function in isolation, with a known input and expected output.
7808d71eb2.wrong: A unit test verifies one specific behaviour of the function in isolation. It doesn't train models, replace logging or measure production traffic.

8f57751be6.question: A developer needs the average value of every element in a NumPy array before passing the r...
8f57751be6.right: np.mean() with no axis averages every element in the array.
8f57751be6.wrong: Use np.mean() without an axis to average all elements. reshape changes the shape, unique finds distinct values, and stack joins arrays.

27be2482ad.question: A 2,000-token document is split into 500-token chunks with 100-token overlap. What does th...
27be2482ad.right: Overlap repeats the edge of one chunk at the start of the next, so ideas split at a boundary stay together.
27be2482ad.wrong: Overlap preserves shared context between neighbouring chunks. It actually adds chunks, and it has no effect on metadata or embedding size.

b207d77f4d.question: A DataFrame should keep rows where score is at least 0.8 and status equals 'approved'. Whi...
b207d77f4d.right: Each condition is in parentheses and combined with &, which is how pandas does element-wise AND.
b207d77f4d.wrong: Use (df['score'] >= 0.8) & (df['status'] == 'approved'). and/or fail on whole Series, and without parentheses & binds before the comparisons.

395364f873.question: An embedding job fails for one document, and the developer needs to identify that document...
395364f873.right: A safe ID (like a document ID or hash) pinpoints the failure without leaking the content.
395364f873.wrong: Log a safe identifier such as the document ID. Logging the content leaks confidential data, and logging the API secret is worse.

df0854da1d.question: A simple keyword retriever treats punctuation as separate token variations. A preprocessin...
df0854da1d.right: Stripping punctuation makes 'error,' and 'error' the same token, so trivial variations stop blocking matches.
df0854da1d.wrong: It reduces superficial token variations, so 'error.' matches 'error'. It doesn't create semantic understanding and it shrinks the vocabulary rather than growing it.

9ccefb8c4e.question: A RAG system returns excellent documents for each individual query, but the final context ...
9ccefb8c4e.right: Removing near-duplicates (or using MMR) frees up context space for different, useful evidence.
9ccefb8c4e.wrong: Deduplicate or diversify the candidates before building the context. More sources, more overlap or a higher temperature add more repetition, not less.

c89ffb05eb.question: Which situation is most suitable for query rewriting?
c89ffb05eb.right: Rewriting helps when the user's wording is vague or doesn't match the document vocabulary.
c89ffb05eb.wrong: Query rewriting suits vague, incomplete or mismatched queries. If retrieval is already perfect, rewriting adds nothing; it also doesn't touch output length or embedding size.

674914e27e.question: What is the main purpose of Retrieval-Augmented Generation?
674914e27e.right: RAG retrieves relevant information and gives it to the model as context, so answers are grounded in real sources.
674914e27e.wrong: RAG supplies retrieved information as context so the model's answer is grounded. It doesn't fine-tune the model or replace it with a search engine.

8ce0b64d81.question: A documentation assistant receives the query "Why isn't it working after I changed the con...
8ce0b64d81.right: Resolve 'it' to the API gateway and rewrite the query, so retrieval searches for what the user actually means.
8ce0b64d81.wrong: Resolve the reference using the conversation and rewrite the query around the API gateway. Searching for the literal word 'it' finds nothing useful.

56405564ab.question: Which statement best describes a vector database?
56405564ab.right: A vector database indexes embeddings for fast nearest-neighbour (similarity) search.
56405564ab.wrong: A vector database is built for searching numerical vectors by similarity. It doesn't generate answers, and transactional SQL is a relational database's job.

45560f94c2.question: A production search pipeline combines BM25 and dense retrieval. BM25 performs well for pro...
45560f94c2.right: RRF merges rankings but doesn't remove duplicates. Deduplicate or use diversity-aware selection (such as MMR) after fusion.
45560f94c2.wrong: Add deduplication or diversity-aware selection after fusion. Tweaking the RRF constant doesn't remove duplicates, and dropping BM25 loses the exact-ID matches.

b6ec1b5cdd.question: A company's HR chatbot receives the query: "How many days can I take for parental leave?" ...
b6ec1b5cdd.right: Rewriting the query into the policy's own terms closes the vocabulary gap that makes search miss the section.
b6ec1b5cdd.wrong: Test query rewriting first, into the policy's terminology. The problem is a wording mismatch; temperature and embedding size don't change that.

ac977ac98e.question: A team adds HYDE to a RAG system and observes better recall but more irrelevant results. W...
ac977ac98e.right: The hypothetical answer may wander into concepts the user didn't ask about, pulling in off-topic documents.
ac977ac98e.wrong: HyDE's generated document can introduce ideas the user didn't mean, so recall rises but precision drops. It doesn't modify the source documents.

435ae2d9cc.question: A RAG architecture currently follows: Query → Dense Retrieval → Top-20 → LLM. Evaluation s...
435ae2d9cc.right: Separate the steps: retrieve broadly, re-rank, pick the strongest evidence and check grounding, instead of passing all 20.
435ae2d9cc.wrong: Use candidate retrieval followed by re-ranking, evidence-aware selection and grounding checks. A bigger top-k or bigger chunks add more noise for the model.

e208d8b418.question: What is the basic idea behind HYDE?
e208d8b418.right: HyDE asks the LLM to write a hypothetical answer, then searches with that answer's embedding.
e208d8b418.wrong: HyDE generates a hypothetical document for the query and uses its embedding for retrieval. It isn't averaging embeddings or a keyword-only query.

63409c1917.question: An enterprise RAG system uses BM25, dense retrieval, query rewriting, RRF, and a cross-enc...
63409c1917.right: Recall is fine; the passages that reach the model lack enough evidence. Fix context selection and add grounding checks.
63409c1917.wrong: Investigate final context selection and grounding validation after re-ranking. More retrievers won't help when the chosen passages don't support the claims.

d0b59e1245.question: A technical RAG system retrieves the correct paragraph but also returns several unrelated ...
d0b59e1245.right: A semantic re-ranker scores each candidate against the query and pushes the truly relevant paragraph to the top.
d0b59e1245.wrong: Apply a semantic re-ranker to the candidates. More BM25 results or bigger chunks add more keyword noise rather than fixing the order.

f871c97fa2.question: A user asks, "What changed in the authentication process between version 2 and version 3?"...
f871c97fa2.right: Splitting the question into v2 and v3 subqueries across the right sources, then fusing and re-ranking, gives balanced evidence.
f871c97fa2.wrong: Break it into comparison subqueries, search the relevant sources, fuse and re-rank. A bigger top-k on the original query still returns mostly v3 documents.

e4307354b1.question: What does Reciprocal Rank Fusion primarily combine?
e4307354b1.right: RRF merges ranked lists using each document's rank position, not its raw score.
e4307354b1.wrong: RRF combines ranked result lists from different retrievers, using rank positions. It doesn't merge embeddings or token probabilities.

408506b9ad.question: A RAG application uses 200-token chunks with no overlap. Answers are technically relevant ...
408506b9ad.right: Overlap or boundary-aware chunking keeps conditions that cross a section edge in the same chunk.
408506b9ad.wrong: Add chunk overlap or boundary-aware chunking. Conditions split across chunks get lost; vector size and top-k don't fix where the cut happens.

7edb1d70ba.question: BM25 primarily determines document relevance using:
7edb1d70ba.right: BM25 scores by term frequency, how rare the term is across documents (IDF), and document length.
7edb1d70ba.wrong: BM25 uses term frequency, document frequency and document length. It's lexical, so it uses no embeddings, attention or LLM probabilities.

95c9610328.question: Why are documents divided into chunks before being stored in a vector database?
95c9610328.right: Chunks are small, focused units that can be embedded and retrieved on their own.
95c9610328.wrong: Chunking creates smaller pieces that can be retrieved independently. It keeps the meaning, produces many embeddings (not one), and has nothing to do with tables.

f08e898690.question: A support system needs to retrieve documents containing exact error codes such as AUTH-401...
f08e898690.right: BM25 nails exact codes like AUTH-4017, dense retrieval finds related ideas, and merging gets you both.
f08e898690.wrong: Combine BM25 and dense retrieval and merge the results. Dense alone can miss exact codes, and BM25 alone misses paraphrased troubleshooting text.

506176ede7.question: A RAG application retrieves 10 documents using dense search and 10 using BM25. Their score...
506176ede7.right: RRF uses rank positions only, so incompatible score scales don't matter.
506176ede7.wrong: Use Reciprocal Rank Fusion. Averaging raw scores on different scales is meaningless, and keeping just one list throws away half the signal.

ce4c8f71f9.question: Which approach is generally considered hybrid retrieval?
ce4c8f71f9.right: Hybrid retrieval combines lexical search (BM25) with dense vector search.
ce4c8f71f9.wrong: Hybrid retrieval means lexical plus dense retrieval, such as BM25 with embeddings. Two LLMs or combined prompts aren't retrieval at all.

ef55dd5898.question: What is the main role of a re-ranker in a RAG pipeline?
ef55dd5898.right: A re-ranker uses a stronger, slower model (often a cross-encoder) to reorder the first-stage candidates.
ef55dd5898.wrong: A re-ranker reorders retrieved candidates with a stronger relevance model. It doesn't generate documents or change the embedding model or context window.

c7ef141d4a.question: What is the main trade-off when increasing chunk size?
c7ef141d4a.right: Bigger chunks carry more context but mix several topics, which blurs similarity matching.
c7ef141d4a.wrong: Larger chunks give more context per chunk but less precise retrieval, because each embedding covers several ideas. It's a trade-off, not a free gain.

20e8664909.question: A knowledge assistant receives a complex query containing several concepts that rarely app...
20e8664909.right: Splitting the question into focused subqueries finds documents for each concept, then the results are merged.
20e8664909.wrong: Generate several focused queries and combine their results. A single top document can't cover concepts that rarely appear together.

f82fed5ad5.question: A legal RAG system uses large chunks because individual clauses depend heavily on surround...
f82fed5ad5.right: Chunk along the document's structure (clauses and sections) and measure retrieval on real legal queries.
f82fed5ad5.wrong: Use structure-aware or semantic chunking and test it on representative queries. Fixed 50-token chunks would split dependent clauses apart.

e0cafa1d26.question: A search system first retrieves 50 candidates using a fast vector index and then applies a...
e0cafa1d26.right: The cheap vector search narrows the set quickly, then the costly cross-encoder only scores the 50 candidates.
e0cafa1d26.wrong: Fast retrieval gathers broad candidates, and the expensive cross-encoder ranks just that small set. Running the cross-encoder on everything would be far too slow.

bb943f6180.question: A retail bot recommends discontinued products because the vector store still holds outdate...
bb943f6180.right: The window controls how much text fits per call, not whether that text is current. Stale data needs a re-index pipeline.
bb943f6180.wrong: A bigger context window can't make stale content current; the store needs a refresh pipeline. The window and the vector store are separate components.

418edb3ba8.question: A researcher agent and a writer agent share a mutable LangGraph state, and a reviewer worr...
418edb3ba8.right: Shared state can be overwritten, so use distinct keys or reducers that define how updates merge.
418edb3ba8.wrong: The risk is real. Nodes do write to shared state, so design the schema with separate keys or reducer functions to stop one agent overwriting another.

18fadafc68.question: A search engineer says BM25 should be replaced everywhere since 'dense embeddings are stri...
18fadafc68.right: Exact identifiers like part numbers or SKUs need lexical matching, which is where BM25 beats embeddings.
18fadafc68.wrong: It backfires on exact part numbers or SKUs. Dense embeddings blur exact tokens, while BM25 matches them precisely. Vague queries are where dense search shines.

810ed11193.question: A colleague argues RAG makes hallucination mathematically impossible because the model 'ju...
810ed11193.right: Retrieval only supplies context; the LLM still generates the answer and can misread, omit or contradict it.
810ed11193.wrong: RAG reduces hallucination but doesn't eliminate it. The LLM still generates text and can misstate what it retrieved.

02121ac2ac.question: A team benchmarks BM25 against dense retrieval and calls dense 'universally better' after ...
02121ac2ac.right: A paraphrase-heavy test set favours semantic matching, so it says little about exact-match queries.
02121ac2ac.wrong: The test set was built for semantic matching, so the result may not hold for exact-match queries like IDs or codes. One benchmark doesn't generalise.

ecd1752855.question: A validation node in a LangGraph workflow fails intermittently, and the team wants exactly...
ecd1752855.right: A retry counter in state lets the conditional edge loop back exactly once, then route to error handling.
ecd1752855.wrong: Keep a retry counter in shared state and have the conditional edge check it. LangGraph doesn't cap a loop at one pass for you, and state can hold counters.

8039678a28.question: An architect is deciding whether to precompute a hybrid index offline or score both retrie...
8039678a28.right: Precomputing makes queries faster but costs storage and re-indexing; scoring at query time is the reverse.
8039678a28.wrong: It's a trade-off between query-time latency and the storage and maintenance cost of a precomputed index. Neither option is always better.

b50783c048.question: An engineer is unsure where query rewriting belongs. Placing it after retrieval instead of...
b50783c048.right: Rewriting after retrieval is pointless: the original query has already chosen the documents.
b50783c048.wrong: The rewrite arrives too late, because retrieval already ran on the original query. Rewriting has to happen before the search to have any effect.

69ee448c2d.question: A finance firm fuses rankings from contracts, emails, and spreadsheets with incompatible s...
69ee448c2d.right: RRF cheaply merges the differently scaled lists, then the expensive cross-encoder re-ranks only the top fused candidates.
69ee448c2d.wrong: Fuse with RRF first, then run the cross-encoder on the top fused results. Averaging raw scores ignores their scales, and cross-encoding everything is wasteful.

f38b0d305b.question: Someone claims RRF and a learned cross-encoder re-ranker 'always produce identical ranking...
f38b0d305b.right: RRF only looks at rank positions, while a trained cross-encoder reads the text, so their rankings often differ.
f38b0d305b.wrong: The claim fails whenever the cross-encoder uses learned relevance signals that rank positions can't capture, which is almost always. They're different methods.

df428e8710.question: Two retrievers return ranked lists on very different score scales (0-1 versus 0-100). A ju...
df428e8710.right: RRF only uses each document's rank position, so a 0-1 scale and a 0-100 scale can't skew the merge.
df428e8710.wrong: RRF merges by rank position, not raw score, so different scales can't bias it. Averaging raw scores lets the 0-100 retriever dominate.

9ae939836d.question: A search tool nails exact product codes but misses paraphrased queries, so an engineer pro...
9ae939836d.right: Manual tagging doesn't scale, and dropping BM25 throws away exact-match strength without fixing paraphrases.
9ae939836d.wrong: The objection: manual tagging can't scale, and removing BM25 loses exact matching without solving paraphrases. Adding dense retrieval alongside BM25 fixes both.

463fccd2af.question: A support bot handles single questions well but struggles with 'and what about the enterpr...
463fccd2af.right: A follow-up only makes sense with earlier turns, so the rewrite must use conversation history, not just the last message.
463fccd2af.wrong: Rewriting has to fold in conversation history. 'And what about the enterprise tier?' means nothing without the previous turn; chunk size and storage aren't the issue.

3c0c48b243.question: An ingestion pipeline chunks files into exactly 100 tokens regardless of structure, and re...
3c0c48b243.right: Structure-aware or semantic chunking with overlap keeps headings and full sentences together.
3c0c48b243.wrong: Switch to structure-aware or semantic chunking with overlap. Indexing whole documents or only first sentences throws away precision or content.

50af1b75cb.question: A company scales its RAG system to 10x more documents using the same chunking and retrieve...
50af1b75cb.right: Settings tuned for a small corpus often need re-tuning at 10x scale, as more chunks start competing for the top spots.
50af1b75cb.wrong: The settings were tuned for the smaller corpus and need re-tuning at scale. More documents means more near-matches competing, so precision drops.

c98c38d803.question: A team wants to retrieve, check if context is sufficient, and retrieve again with a refine...
c98c38d803.right: It needs a loop between retrieval and a sufficiency check, with state counting attempts so the loop stops.
c98c38d803.wrong: Build a conditional loop between retrieval and a sufficiency check, with an attempts counter in state. One fixed call has no way to retry.

0472675ae4.question: A developer edits the LLM's final generated answer text after generation and calls this 'q...
0472675ae4.right: Query rewriting changes the query before retrieval. Editing the answer afterwards changes nothing about what was found.
0472675ae4.wrong: That isn't query rewriting. A rewrite has to change the query before retrieval; editing the final answer doesn't affect which documents were found.

7f26b43a86.question: A developer claims any LangGraph workflow can be rewritten as a plain linear LangChain seq...
7f26b43a86.right: Linear chains only move forward, so cycles, conditional branches and revisited state need a graph.
7f26b43a86.wrong: The claim fails whenever the workflow needs cycles, conditional branches or state across revisits. A linear chain can't loop back.

55583f1ce7.question: A team decomposes one LangChain call into separate retrieval, generation, and validation n...
55583f1ce7.right: For a single-path task with no branching, retries or state, a plain chain is simpler and enough.
55583f1ce7.wrong: The reviewer is right when the task is single-path with no branching, retries or persistent state. Then the graph only adds overhead.

81bb8877f6.question: In LangChain, a 'Retriever' and a 'Chain' are sometimes confused by newcomers. Which disti...
81bb8877f6.right: A retriever only fetches relevant documents; a chain wires retrieval, prompting and generation together.
81bb8877f6.wrong: A Retriever fetches documents, and a Chain composes steps like retrieval and generation. Retrievers don't generate answers or train embeddings.

4b06d9f4a8.question: A team says LangChain and a vector database serve the exact same purpose in an LLM stack, ...
4b06d9f4a8.right: LangChain orchestrates prompts, tools and steps, while the vector database stores and searches embeddings. They complement each other.
4b06d9f4a8.wrong: They do different jobs. LangChain orchestrates prompts and tools, and a vector database stores embeddings for similarity search.

449b156d48.question: A team building an agent that retries a failing tool call up to three times before escalat...
449b156d48.right: Bounded retry with escalation needs a loop, a counter in state and a branch, which LangGraph provides.
449b156d48.wrong: The gap is stateful, cyclic control flow: retry up to three times, then escalate. Plain LangChain can call tools but has no loop or retry counter.

7ba4458f7c.question: A legal system needs exact clause matches and paraphrase tolerance. A vendor proposes dens...
7ba4458f7c.right: Embeddings can blur exact clause wording that BM25 matches precisely, so hybrid fusion covers both needs.
7ba4458f7c.wrong: Dense embeddings can under-represent exact terms, and that's where BM25 shines. For both exact clauses and paraphrases, use hybrid retrieval.

38eb4965a2.question: A chatbot answers benefits questions correctly alone but forgets the health plan mentioned...
38eb4965a2.right: Forgetting something from two turns ago is a memory problem, and more documents can't fix it.
38eb4965a2.wrong: The real gap is memory across turns, not document coverage. The bot needs conversation state that carries the health plan forward.

3258dabe55.question: A legal assistant must loop between drafting and compliance-check nodes until approval, bu...
3258dabe55.right: A LangGraph loop with an iteration counter in state and a conditional edge to human escalation at 5 covers both rules.
3258dabe55.wrong: Use a LangGraph loop with a state counter that routes to a human once it hits 5. A prompt saying 'try up to 5 times' isn't enforceable.

0e812dbbc4.question: An agent remembers a user's stated dietary restriction across many separate sessions spann...
0e812dbbc4.right: Facts that survive across sessions for weeks are long-term memory.
0e812dbbc4.wrong: That's long-term memory: it persists across sessions. Short-term memory lasts only for the current conversation.

65200af9e7.question: In the Model Context Protocol, what is the core relationship between a client and a server...
65200af9e7.right: An MCP client connects to one or more servers, and each server exposes tools, resources or prompts.
65200af9e7.wrong: The client connects to one or more MCP servers, and each server exposes tools, resources or prompts. Servers don't push unsolicited tool calls to clients.

3244194014.question: A production agent occasionally enters a loop calling the same expensive tool repeatedly, ...
3244194014.right: A hard cap on tool calls stops the loop, and alerts on unusual call volume catch it early.
3244194014.wrong: Add a hard limit on tool calls plus monitoring and alerts. A cheaper model still loops, and turning off logging just hides the cost.

55b4fd9fc1.question: In a LangGraph StateGraph, what determines which node executes next after the current node...
55b4fd9fc1.right: The edges leaving a node, including conditional edges evaluated against state, decide what runs next.
55b4fd9fc1.wrong: The outgoing edges decide, and conditional edges check the current state. Order of definition in code doesn't decide it, and nothing is random.

e3bb6afdd4.question: A company wants an agent to read from an internal ticketing system without hardcoding that...
e3bb6afdd4.right: Wrap the ticketing system once as an MCP server, and any MCP-compatible agent can reuse it.

01b85e5db3.right: High, Medium and Low have a natural order, which makes them ordinal.

ae66833cfe.question: Which algorithm uses hyperplanes for classification?

ab42c63d68.question: Which ensemble technique trains models independently and in parallel?
ab42c63d68.right: Bagging trains each model independently on a bootstrap sample, so they can run in parallel.
ab42c63d68.wrong: That's bagging, as in Random Forest. Boosting trains models one after another, and gradient descent is an optimiser, not an ensemble.

1c90ac8f1a.question: Why is feature scaling important before applying K-Means?
1c90ac8f1a.right: K-Means relies on distances, so unscaled large-range features dominate the clustering.
1c90ac8f1a.wrong: Scale because K-Means uses distances and large-range features would dominate. Scaling doesn't choose K or remove outliers.

df37923a86.question: A data scientist notices that the training accuracy is 99% while test accuracy is 62%. Wha...

df37923a86.wrong: It's overfitting: 99% on training but 62% on test. Underfitting would be poor on training data too.

827b068930.question: Cluster: 5 worker nodes each node = 8 cores Spark Submit: --num-executors 5 --executor-cor...

b174ccf837.question: What is the main purpose of an activation function in a neural network?
b174ccf837.right: Without activation functions, stacked layers collapse into one linear function. Non-linearity lets networks learn complex patterns.
b174ccf837.wrong: Activation functions add non-linearity. Without them a deep network behaves like a single linear model.

dd1f63f19d.wrong: Start with the Random Forest (Model A). It does well on tabular data and runs on CPUs, while a deep network needs more compute for similar results.

0af52c9973.wrong: Caching avoids recomputing a DataFrame you use more than once. It doesn't change columns, executors or duplicates.

d4f2c78b78.question: What does a Kafka offset represent?

d4f2c78b78.wrong: An offset is a record's position within a partition. Consumers commit offsets to remember how far they've read.

67f36b4f4f.question: A company is building a sentiment analysis system for customer reviews. The model needs to...
67f36b4f4f.right: A BiLSTM runs one pass forwards and one backwards, so each word sees both earlier and later context.
67f36b4f4f.wrong: A BiLSTM uses two passes, forward and backward, to capture past and future context. It still uses embeddings, and a plain LSTM only sees past tokens.

629dace627.question: Correct the order of execution during a SQL Execution?

629dace627.wrong: The logical order is FROM, then WHERE, then SELECT. SELECT is written first but evaluated after the rows are chosen.

6f29c3761e.question: A DataFrame has 1,000 partitions. You want to increase them to 2,000. Which operation shou...

6f29c3761e.wrong: Use repartition(2000). coalesce only reduces partitions, so coalesce(2000) on 1,000 partitions does nothing.

1d0b06f1cb.question: The key advantage of an RNN over a basic feed-forward ANN for sequence data is:
1d0b06f1cb.right: An RNN carries a hidden state from step to step, which acts as memory of earlier inputs.
1d0b06f1cb.wrong: An RNN keeps a hidden state with information from previous steps. It still has parameters and needs training, and it handles variable-length input.

06d659af7f.question: You have: Orders table → 500 GB Customer table → 5 MB What is the Best optimization you wo...
06d659af7f.right: A 5 MB table fits on every executor, so broadcasting it avoids shuffling the 500 GB orders table.
06d659af7f.wrong: Broadcast the customer table. Sending a 5 MB copy to every executor avoids shuffling 500 GB; repartitioning would shuffle both tables.

a2ab08d466.question: An order-service publishes order events to Kafka. A separate inventory-service needs to re...
a2ab08d466.right: Inventory-service reads events, so it's a consumer of the topic.
a2ab08d466.wrong: It's a Consumer. The order-service is the producer, and the topic and partition are where events are stored, not the reader.

a5a7d1a0bf.question: Spark job generated 40,000 parquet files. What is the best optimization before writing the...

a5a7d1a0bf.wrong: Use coalesce() to reduce the number of partitions, and so the number of files, before writing. repartition(50000) would create even more files.

76094f54a1.right: coalesce() merges existing partitions on the same executors, so no full shuffle is needed.
76094f54a1.wrong: Use coalesce(), which merges partitions without a full shuffle. repartition() always shuffles, even when reducing.

eb2caadd19.question: An ANN neuron has: Inputs = [2, 3] Weights = [0.5, 0.2] Bias = 0.1 What is the pre-activat...

eb2caadd19.wrong: It's 1.7: multiply each input by its weight, add them, then add the bias. 2×0.5 + 3×0.2 + 0.1 = 1.0 + 0.6 + 0.1.

affdb90831.question: A DataFrame requires 30 minutes to generate and is used 5 times. Caching it: memory usage ...
affdb90831.right: Caching is a trade-off: 30 minutes saved on each of 5 reuses versus the memory the cache takes up.
affdb90831.wrong: Weigh the recomputation cost against the memory used. A 30-minute job reused 5 times usually justifies caching, but never 'always' or 'never'.

f2bd9db502.question: Two tables: A = 1 TB B = 500 GB Both are joined on customer_id. One customer represents 40...

a03aba2b48.right: A few tasks running far longer because a few keys hold millions of rows is data skew.

4e565ab7fa.question: Which situation is most suitable for caching?
4e565ab7fa.right: Cache when an expensive result is reused several times; that's when it pays for its memory.
4e565ab7fa.wrong: Caching suits an expensive DataFrame that's reused several times. Caching something used once only costs memory and time.

42140be745.question: Which technique can be used to handle severe data skew?
42140be745.right: Salting adds a random prefix to hot keys, spreading their rows over many partitions.
42140be745.wrong: Use salting to spread hot keys across partitions. More driver memory or collecting data doesn't help the overloaded tasks on the executors.

a25b9c00f2.question: Which is BAD practice you would consider during spark processing?
a25b9c00f2.right: Caching data you only use once spends memory and time for no benefit.
a25b9c00f2.wrong: Caching a DataFrame used only once is the bad practice. Caching reused DataFrames and small lookup tables is good practice.

15b4f07c9b.question: Cluster: 50 cores available Spark submit: --num-executors 2 --executor-cores 2 Problem?
15b4f07c9b.right: 2 executors × 2 cores = 4 of 50 cores used, so the cluster is badly underused.
15b4f07c9b.wrong: The cluster is underutilised: 2 × 2 = 4 cores out of 50. Raise the executors or cores to use the capacity.

ee3ad91998.question: A telecom company has 20,000 customer records with features such as age, monthly bill, con...

98c1670839.question: A VNet has 10.0.1.0/24 (web) and 10.0.2.0/24 (database) subnets. Why separate them?

707a9dcd2e.right: An image is a template; each docker run creates a new, independent container from it.

75b56f6fc5.question: A customer says "My phone rang but the call dropped as soon as I picked up." Which call ph...

5869cd53ef.question: A Platinum SLA customer experiences 15 min of downtime in a month (SLA allows 4.3 min). Wh...

5869cd53ef.wrong: It's an SLA breach: 15 minutes against 4.3 allowed, which triggers a penalty or credit note. The customer isn't at fault.

09bd6c4cc5.right: In VoLTE, SIP sets up and controls the call and RTP carries the actual voice.
09bd6c4cc5.wrong: Signaling is SIP and media is RTP. SS7 and TDM belong to legacy circuit-switched networks.

b9ca63d87f.question: A customer upgrades from 4G to 5G and sees latency drop from 50 ms to 5 ms. What is the PR...

2065a399f7.question: A CDR shows a 322-second call. Tariff is ₹1.00/min with rounding up to next minute. What i...

7218dd1a8b.question: A GenAI NOC summary says "~30 customers affected" but a PON can serve up to 128 ONTs. What...
7218dd1a8b.right: A PON can serve up to 128 ONTs, so '~30 customers' likely understates how many were hit.

06e2ac6564.question: An engineer needs a VM accessible from the internet but without exposing it directly. What...

a5e220dba3.question: A postpaid bill shows a "pro-rata charge" because the plan was activated on the 15th. What...

32ee000c7e.question: A developer asks why TCP is used for web and UDP for VoIP. What is the correct reasoning?

1509dc3f23.question: An application requires different database URLs for development, testing, and production. ...

0f9d83c67d.question: A telecom employee is asked to classify "customer complaint handling." Which is correct?

7bd8582e5a.question: A user reports "no internet, but calls work" on 4G. Where is the MOST likely issue?

7bd8582e5a.wrong: The core network's user-plane data path is the most likely issue. Calls prove the access network and phone work; the data path specifically is failing.

b4a34ef48a.question: A prepaid customer makes calls with ₹0 balance. Which system is likely malfunctioning?

2885e01b9b.question: A data center uses 200 kW total power and 150 kW for IT equipment. What is the PUE?

7b1903b3e5.wrong: Correlate the alarms first to find the root cause. Restarting everything or closing tickets without a diagnosis can make things worse.

ca041ef4cc.question: A NOC engineer sees alarms from "gNB-DEL-01" and "AMF-MUM-01." Which generation is this?

da68fc32e7.right: An automated retraining pipeline retrains on new data when enough arrives, with no manual steps.
da68fc32e7.wrong: Build an automated retraining pipeline triggered by new data. Deleting the model or editing predictions by hand doesn't scale.
